title: Single-page checkout lifts conversion 5.6% — but the win is on mobile web, not the app
subtitle: Four weeks, 620k sessions: ship the new checkout to web now, and give the app team one more iteration before it goes to 100%.
summary: A four-week A/B test (620k sessions) of a single-page checkout against the current three-step flow lifted session conversion from 3.40% to 3.59% (+5.6%, 95% CI +2.9% to +8.3%). Nearly all of the gain is on mobile web; the native apps are neutral. We recommend shipping to web with a 5% holdout, iterating on the app, and planning on about $20M of annualised revenue rather than the $53M point estimate.
key_findings: Session conversion rose from 3.40% to 3.59%, a +5.6% relative lift (95% CI +2.9% to +8.3%).
Mobile web lift was +14.2% (CI +7.9% to +20.8%); iOS (+0.6%) and Android (−1.2%) apps were neutral.
AOV fell 1.3%, inside the −3% guardrail, mainly because protection-plan attach dropped from 6.8% to 5.9%.
Support contacts per 1k orders fell 7%; payment errors rose only on Android because of a ZIP+4 AVS bug.
Recommended FP&A planning figure is about $20M annualised web revenue, versus a $53M naive point estimate.
